Run a differential-abundance analysis

Source: R/mp_da.R
mp_run_da.Rd

Tests every taxon for a difference in abundance between the levels of group.by, with one or several methods, and returns a long, tidy table ready for mp_diff(). Running several methods in one call and looking at where they agree (mp_diff(plot.type = "consensus")) is the recommended practice: independent benchmarks show that differential-abundance methods frequently disagree, and that adjusting for confounders matters.

Usage

mp_run_da(
  object,
  group.by = NULL,
  method = "wilcox",
  groups = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  adjust = NULL,
  random = NULL,
  pairwise = FALSE,
  tax.level = NULL,
  prevalence = 0.1,
  p.adjust.method = "BH",
  engine.args = list(),
  verbose = getOption("micropubr.verbose", FALSE)
)

Arguments

object

A phyloseq::phyloseq or (Tree)SummarizedExperiment object with counts.

group.by

Sample-metadata column defining the groups.

method

One or more of "wilcox", "lm", "ancombc2", "deseq2" and "aldex2". Several methods are run on the same design and stacked.

groups

Optional subset of group.by levels to compare (at least two). The first is the reference unless reference is given, so groups = c("Control", "Treatment") is the classic two-group comparison.

reference

Reference level. Defaults to the first of groups, or to the first level of group.by.

adjust

Optional metadata columns to adjust for (covariates or confounders such as age, sex or medication). Used by "lm", "ancombc2" and "deseq2"; the other methods warn and run unadjusted.

random

Optional metadata column identifying repeated measures (for example a subject id), modelled as a random intercept by "lm" and "ancombc2".

pairwise

If TRUE, test every pair of levels; by default each level is compared with reference.

tax.level

Optional rank to agglomerate to first.

prevalence

Minimum fraction of samples a taxon must be detected in to be tested (default 0.1, as in ANCOM-BC2).

p.adjust.method

Multiple-testing correction, applied within each method and contrast (default "BH"); see stats::p.adjust().

engine.args

Extra arguments for the underlying engine, e.g. list(n_cl = 4) for ANCOMBC::ancombc2(). With several methods, nest them by method: list(ancombc2 = list(n_cl = 4)).

verbose

Print the methods used.

Value

A data frame with one row per feature, contrast and method: feature (display label), feature_id (taxon id), contrast, method, log2FC, lfcSE, pvalue, padj, mean (mean relative abundance), robust (passed ANCOM-BC2's pseudo-count sensitivity analysis; NA for other methods) and structural_zero (absent from one group of the contrast, so not tested). The design is recorded in attr(x, "mp_da") and used by mp_diff() and mp_methods().

Methods

"wilcox"

Wilcoxon rank-sum test on centred log-ratio (CLR) transformed counts (pseudocount 1). Dependency-free and fast, but it cannot adjust for covariates. lfcSE is the Welch standard error of the mean CLR difference.

"lm"

Linear model on CLR-transformed counts with the adjust covariates as additional terms. With random, a linear mixed model with a random intercept per level of random (requires lmerTest; Satterthwaite degrees of freedom).

"ancombc2"

ANCOM-BC2 (package ANCOMBC): a log-linear model with correction for sample-specific sampling fractions, detection of structural zeros (taxa absent from a whole group) and a pseudo-count sensitivity analysis, reported in the robust column. Supports adjust and random; with pairwise = TRUE the contrasts control the mixed directional FDR.

"deseq2"

DESeq2 negative-binomial Wald test with "poscounts" size factors, which tolerate the many zeros of microbiome data. Supports adjust.

"aldex2"

ALDEx2 Welch's t-test on Monte-Carlo CLR instances, run separately for each contrast. Cannot adjust for covariates.

"ancombc" is accepted as an alias of "ancombc2"; the original ANCOM-BC has been superseded by its authors.

Fold changes are always on the log2 scale and positive when a feature is more abundant in the first-named group of the contrast ("B vs A" means higher in B). ANCOM-BC2's natural-log estimates are converted.

See also

mp_diff() to plot the result.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(GlobalPatterns, package = "phyloseq")
gp <- phyloseq::subset_samples(GlobalPatterns,
                               SampleType %in% c("Feces", "Skin", "Tongue"))
